editorial:
Imagine waking up in a world where people are randomly turning into animals. That is the wild setup you get here. You follow François, a dad who is desperate to save his wife after she transforms. He and his son, Émile, head into the woods to find the other mutated people. The vibe is a mix of a family road trip and a weird sci-fi mystery. It does not feel like a typical monster movie; instead, it feels more like a story about a father and son trying to figure out their relationship while the world falls apart around them.

What really works is the acting and the strange, cool visuals of the animal-people. The pacing starts slow but picks up as they get deeper into the forest. One downside is that some parts might feel a bit too quiet for people who want non-stop action. However, if you like stories that make you think and feel, you will love this. You should definitely stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see all the detail in the forest, or grab the 4K Blu-ray if you like owning physical copies of unique films.
endingExplained: At the end, you discover that the mutation is not a disease, but a new way for humans to evolve and live in harmony with nature. Émile eventually transforms into a bird, completing his journey. Instead of fighting the change, he embraces it. The movie wraps up by showing that letting go is the only way to find peace, as the humans and animals merge into one new society in the wild.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves unique sci-fi stories and family dramas.
